title: Aim
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: The same widget as Premise (WO-0021, already in design on the floor): unspoken assumptions quoted from the thinking stream and dropped when the reply states them.
stamps.subject: Unsaid

stamps.reason: The same widget as Strays (WO-0019, at shipping): the servers this session started, by port, with a stop verb; a liveness probe and a toast are a feature of that card, not a new one.
stamps.subject: Harbour

stamps.reason: Rejected before and nothing has changed: the card cannot show that a gear change helped, a low gear may quietly reason worse, and whether a per-step effort change spends the prompt cache is still unmeasured.
stamps.subject: Gearbox

stamps.reason: Rejected before and nothing has changed: the engine already defers MCP tools, so the saving is a few cached built-in descriptions, bought with the risk that Claude does not reach for a tool it cannot see.
stamps.subject: Attic

stamps.reason: Word overlap on a half-typed prompt cannot tell a repeated question from a similar-looking one, most coding prompts depend on the conversation they were asked in so the old answer is rarely reusable, and the price is a card that flickers with every burst of typing.
stamps.subject: Deja vu

stamps.reason: The reverse of wager-widget built on the suggestion nextup-widget also plays with: a novelty score that wears off in a day, paid for by giving up the Tab suggestion, which is useful every turn.
stamps.subject: Envelope

stamps.reason: It writes a permanent line into history other people share, the model rather than the widget writes it so the measured figures are not guaranteed, and the numbers are receipt-widget's; permanence is out of proportion to a line most teams would ask to have removed.
stamps.subject: Colophon

stamps.reason: Aim is the only idea that is new, works with the API as it is and earns a mention: it names the cluster, account or database a command is aimed at inside the permission dialog, which stakes-widget (git loss only) cannot, at no token cost.

No blocking fault: every hook and call is in the 2.1.289 types file, all six states are drawn and fit 36 and 16, the nine risks of the idea are settled, 120 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 14 notes in spec-notes.md.

Built aim-widget: a tool.check hook on Bash and PowerShell that names the kube context, aws profile, gcloud project, terraform workspace or database a asked command reaches in the dialog's reason, with a resting card of ambient targets, production words and 15 acceptance tests; the checker passes.

Well built and the live run was good, but the command reader names a confident wrong target in seven shapes (psql -hHOST and PGSERVICE read as localhost; pushd/Set-Location, subshells, unset, kubectl --cluster/--server, a setter under -chdir, heredoc bodies and comments); each must become not known or the right target; see inspection.md.

Fixed all seven inspection findings in the reading of a command (psql attached flags and PGSERVICE/PGHOSTADDR, pushd/Set-Location, subshell scope, unset and env -u, kubectl cluster flags, setters under -chdir, heredoc bodies and comments) with tests added to A5, A7, A8 and A9

The seven earlier findings are fixed and the live run is good, but a command continued over lines with a backslash (or a PowerShell backtick) loses the flags on its later lines and names the ambient target instead of the one given (--context, --profile, -h, --project, --kubeconfig, a leading AWS_PROFILE=); also a kube context repointed earlier in the line (aws eks update-kubeconfig, gcloud get-credentials, kubectx) and a gcloud configuration switch are not seen; see inspection.md.

Fixed the second inspection: continued lines join before reading, commands that repoint kubectl or switch the gcloud configuration make later aims not known, and the notes (lone &, PowerShell call operator, AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE, TF_DATA_DIR, psql positional database) are settled with tests in A5 to A9.

The second inspection's findings are fixed and the live run is good, but a command substitution in the middle of a command ($( ), backticks, <( )) drops the flags after it and names the ambient target instead of the one given (--context, --profile, --kubeconfig); braces inside a word (jsonpath={.x}, xargs -I{}, pod/{a,b}) and a backslash-escaped quote or semicolon do the same, and a setter inside a subshell is forgotten; see inspection.md.

Fixed the third inspection: substitutions, process substitutions and backticks mid-command now let the outer command carry on, braces separate only as their own word, backslash and PowerShell backtick escape, subshell setters carry out, plus the four notes.

Within the ruling: every finding of inspections one to three stays fixed across about 230 replayed command lines, the live run is good, plain commands name the right target or not known, the checker passes; six notes on rarer shapes in inspection.md, none blocking.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
